r0.why: Definition [1], smaller requirement often omitted [3], submatrix vs minor terminology [10].

r1.why: (i,j) minor by deleting row i and column j, M_(i,j) [4][5]; cofactor via (-1)^(i+j), C_(i,j) [6]; M2,3 example [7].

r2.why: First minors for cofactors, determinant and inverse [2]; transpose of cofactor matrix is adjugate/classical adjoint [16]; zeroth minor is determinant [12].

r3.why: m x n matrix, integer 0<k<=m, k<=n [8]; k x k minor of order k by deleting m-k rows, n-k columns [9]; order zero often 1 [11].

r4.why: Rank r gives a nonzero r x r minor and all larger minors zero over a field [17]; basic minor defined [20].

r5.why: Principal minor I=J [18], i leading principal minors [19], Hermitian definiteness tests [21], Sylvester's criterion for details [22].

r6.why: Wedge-product treatment [24], k x k minors as components of k-vectors [25], coefficients -13,-7,5 agree with earlier minors [26][27].
